gamedemo package¶

Submodules¶

gamedemo.game module¶

game.py¶

This module contains the Game class that implements the actual game mechanics as well as the __main__ construct to make the game runnable.

class gamedemo.game.Game(player1: Player, player2: Player)[source]¶

Bases: object

The game class implements the game mechanics for this demo. To understand the way the game works, read the documentation for the run() method.

run()[source]¶

This method implements the game mechanics. The game loops until one of the players runs out of health. Every turn, one of the players is randomly chosen to attack. We call the attack() method on that player’s weapon. The damage dealt by this attack is applied to the player by calling gamedemo.player.Player.take_hit().

gamedemo.game.run()[source]¶

Note: this function looks slightly different in the videos. I changed this to make it easier to run the project. See __main__.py for instructions.

class gamedemo.player.Player(name, weapon)[source]¶

Bases: object

The Player class represents the characters in the game.

Variables:

health – The current health of the character. Starts at 100. Once it reaches 0, we’re dead.

property is_alive¶

True if health is larger than 0, False otherwise

take_hit(damage)[source]¶

This method gets called when the player takes a hit from the opponent’s weapon :param damage: The damage dealt. This will be substracted from health. :return: The new value of health.

gamedemo.weapons module¶

weapons.py¶

This module contains classes for Weapons.

class gamedemo.weapons.FireBreath[source]¶

Bases: Weapon

FireBreath is a weapon only wielded by dragons or wizards. It can deal a lot of damage, but it also has its drawbacks. There is a 30% chance that the attack will not work, and after a successful attack you will need to wait a while before you will be able to breath fire again.

attack()[source]¶

This method should return a tuple (damage, text): how much damage was dealt and what text to output. Text is a format string with placeholders for attacker and defender.

A primitive close-range weapon. It deals either 5 or 10 damage with a 50/50 chance.

Module contents¶

Demo Project: Game¶

This project serves mainly as an example project for my

Pluralsight video course.

The idea is to simulate a very simple role-playing game where two characters fight. The game mechanics are controlled by the game.Game class and the characters are Player instances, each of which has a Weapon to attack with.

The scenario we will try to simulate is of an old-fashioned knight fighting a fire-breathing dragon.

Running this project¶

You can run this project with the command “python -m gamedemo”. Make sure you are located at the project toplevel directory (outside the package).
